scope: Engine-side heater takeoffs and PCM ECT construction; full vehicle hoses and gauge-sender mounting remain incomplete

sources.title: Ford 1994 4.9L ECT location and heater-elbow illustration A20800-A
sources.review: Image visually reviewed: ECT screws into the metal heater elbow at the thermostat outlet. Separate bent heater-return tube enters the pump. Drawing is not dimensioned.

sources.title: Ford ECT description, operation and dry-seal thread illustration
sources.review: Two-lead negative-temperature-coefficient thermistor; PCM uses its input for fueling, EGR and ignition. Thread image visually specifies 3/8-18 NPTF-SPL. Saved parts page lists E1AZ12A648A; no production dimensions taken from that listing.

sources.title: 1994 Ford EVTM: separate ECT and gauge sender circuits and locations
sources.review: C183 is the two-wire ECT at the thermostat housing. C150 is the separate RH-side engine gauge sender; circuit 39 R/W and body ground feed the gauge. Gauge diagram marks 74 ohms cold and 9.7 ohms hot without assigning temperatures. Location drawing is schematic, not a coordinate reference.

sources.title: Owner engine-bay photos: paired heater hoses
sources.review: Both photos visually reviewed. Two red-orange hoses run between firewall/heater region and front engine. Exact endpoints and dimensions are partly occluded; photos do not justify an installed hose centerline or a bleed tee.
Existing saved catalog review lists 18767 for heater-to-thermostat and heater-to-water-pump in the five-speed manual branch. It establishes replacement application, not these tube dimensions.

manual_branch_exclusion.reason: The radiator bleed tee routing procedure explicitly applies to E4OD transmission vehicles; not applied to this manual truck.

gauge_sender.reason: Existing cylinder head has no verified wet jacket or sender bore; mounting deferred instead of placing sender in a dry/combustion/oil passage.

provisional_geometry_mm.limits: All dimensions and orientation are current-CAD fit choices. Only ECT thread designation and two-terminal architecture are sourced.

connectivity.supply: Existing coolant outlet secondary bore to attached metal elbow to open heater-supply interface
connectivity.return: Open heater-return interface through attached metal elbow and drilled pump-housing port into existing coolant chamber
connectivity.wet_sensor: ECT probe projects into elbow fluid cavity; no water passes through the sealed electrical interior
connectivity.checks: Four swept/straight bore probes tested for obstructions against candidate and installed solids. These prove geometric open paths, not coolant flow rate or factory routing.
unfinished: Actual vehicle hoses, clamps and harness

integration.no_outlet_replacement: Elbow inserts in existing open secondary bore; original outlet remains unchanged.
